## 1. The operational quantity

A detector \(E=(E_i)\) acts on a finite-dimensional system \(A\) and outputs a classical label. The input description explicitly lists the matrices \(E_i\), whose real and imaginary entries are rational, with

\[
E_i>0,\qquad \sum_iE_i=I.
\]

An experiment prepares one of two faithful states \(\rho_{AR},\sigma_{AR}\), applies the detector to \(A\), and retains the finite quantum reference \(R\). Both candidate detectors are evaluated on the same hypotheses and reference.

For output states \(X,Y\), define the quantum Chernoff distance in bits,

\[
C(X,Y)
=
-\log_2\min_{0\le s\le1}\operatorname{Tr}X^sY^{1-s}.
\]

For independent repetitions, this is the optimal asymptotic exponent of the equal-prior decision error. The operational identification comes from the quantum Chernoff theorem. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

The full benchmark is

\[
V_C(P,Q)
=
\sup_{\substack{\dim R<\infty\\ \rho,\sigma>0}}
\left[
C(Q_R\rho,Q_R\sigma)
-
C(P_R\rho,P_R\sigma)
\right],
\]

where \(E_R=E\otimes\mathrm{id}_R\).

Thus \(V_C(P,Q)\) measures the greatest improvement in binary-decision exponent obtainable by replacing \(P\) with \(Q\), allowing any finite retained reference.

A particularly useful subclass is governed by the square-root affinity

\[
a_E(\rho,\sigma)
=
\operatorname{Tr}
\sqrt{E_R\rho}\sqrt{E_R\sigma},
\]

and the benchmark

\[
V_{\mathrm{bal}}(P,Q)
=
\sup_{\substack{\dim R<\infty\\ \rho,\sigma>0}}
\log_2\frac{a_P(\rho,\sigma)}{a_Q(\rho,\sigma)}.
\]

This subclass has a direct physical realization. Add one retained fair classical bit and prepare

\[
\widetilde\rho=\frac12(\rho\oplus\sigma),
\qquad
\widetilde\sigma=\frac12(\sigma\oplus\rho).
\]

The Chernoff moment of this pair is convex and symmetric about \(s=1/2\), so its minimum occurs there. Consequently,

\[
C(E_R\widetilde\rho,E_R\widetilde\sigma)
=
-\log_2 a_E(\rho,\sigma).
\]

The fair-bit construction therefore realizes \(V_{\mathrm{bal}}\) as an actual discrimination-exponent advantage. It gives

\[
V_{\mathrm{bal}}(P,Q)\le V_C(P,Q).
\]

I do not assume their numerical values are equal.

### The quantities remain finite

Allowing different reference marginals in the two hypotheses might initially suggest that the reference could make these quantities infinite. Strict positivity of the detector effects prevents that.

## 4. The finite-memory evaluator is constructed and executed

For a specified reference dimension \(r\), introduce the two faithful input density matrices and positive square-root variables for every detector output block:

\[
X_{E,i}^2=(E_R\rho)_i,
\qquad
Y_{E,i}^2=(E_R\sigma)_i.
\]

The affinity becomes

\[
a_E=\sum_i\operatorname{Tr}X_{E,i}Y_{E,i}.
\]

For a rational threshold \(z\), the question

\[
\exists\,\rho,\sigma>0:
\qquad a_P>z\,a_Q
\]

is an existential real-algebraic feasibility problem. The implementation splits complex matrices into real coordinates and uses positivity factorizations; at each fixed threshold, the constraints have degree at most two.

Exact real quantifier elimination decides the threshold question. Bisection computes the affinity-ratio supremum, and rational logarithm bounds compute the benchmark in bits. The construction handles the open faithful domain without assuming that the supremum is attained.

I implemented this interface and a certified optimizer. The completed examples include:

| Source detector | Target detector | Original reference dimension | Certified advantage, bits |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Fair coin | Noisy \(Z\) measurement | 1 | \([0.207490,\;0.207552]\) |
| Noisy \(Z\) measurement | Fair coin | 1 | \([0,\;0.000092]\) |

The first exact supremum is

\[
\log_2\frac{2}{\sqrt3}
\approx0.20751875.
\]

It is approached by opposite pure inputs, so this example checks the treatment of a boundary supremum. The physical balancing operation adds a retained bit.

Every positive model in the completed optimizer examples was checked against the exact polynomial constraints. Other exploratory solver runs timed out; their receipts remain explicitly `UNKNOWN`. The general termination theorem uses exact real quantifier elimination, while practical timeouts are computational limits of those runs.

The memory impossibility now follows directly. If a total algorithm supplied an approximately sufficient dimension budget, the finite-memory evaluator could optimize every dimension up to that budget and distinguish the compiled zero-versus-one family.

7. What this adds, and what remains distinct

A source comparison established that Astra N676 already contains the qualitative Petz/Chernoff order equivalence, the balancing operation, and the quadratic endpoint classification. Those are prior results, and the report attributes them explicitly to the 
pinned governing source.

The additions established here are:

An explicit faithful source-to-affinity conversion with an absolute margin independent of the unknown reference dimension.
Fixed-additive-accuracy impossibility for the two specified discrimination benchmarks.
An implemented algebraic finite-reference optimizer and the resulting impossibility of computing approximately sufficient reference memory.
A dimension-independent finite-copy conversion with predetermined repetition counts.
Calibration, preparation, and compiled-test robustness with stated physical costs.

The comparison with current primary research preserves its actual operational settings. The generalized Chernoff theorem treats composite hypotheses drawn from convex tensor-stable sets; the present experiment uses fixed-pair independent copies. Hirche’s current estimation work supplies related coherent-reference and channel-order machinery. Neither substitutes for the quantitative margin constructed here.

+1

Likewise, the 2026 capacity paper proves ordinary-capacity QMA hardness using circuit descriptions, while its undecidability result concerns a restricted entanglement-assisted one-shot zero-error classical capacity. Those results do not resolve ordinary unassisted quantum-capacity approximation, and neither does this continuation. 
arxiv.org

The new principle is precise: finite quantum decision problems can have computable optima at every specified memory size, computable repetition and precision requirements for positive witnesses, yet no computable memory budget guaranteeing even a coarse approximation to their unrestricted optimum. The construction identifies the resource carrying that obstruction and proves that its useful size cannot be universally bounded by an algorithm.
